wisata.description.danau-bundala-alani: Behind the beauty of Lake Bundala Alani, there is a historical story that developed in the community. Long ago, there lived a beautiful girl named Lemelu. From infancy, she was part of a meaningful story. One day, when Lemelu was still a toddler and defecated, her mother asked for help from a young man named Anggabule to fetch seven pieces of balande wood leaves as a cleanser because there was no water. In return, the mother promised that when Lemelu grew up, she would be married to Anggabule. However, fate said otherwise. When Lemelu grew into an adult, she was proposed to by the son of King Balalon. Anggabule, feeling betrayed, tried to thwart the wedding, but all his efforts were in vain. On the wedding day, Anggabule played the role of a drum beater. While the event was festive, Anggabule went under the house to shake the chicken basket containing sea and land animals. This caused all the animals to scatter, creating a huge chaos. Near midnight, Anggabule went down and pulled out grass (mbembelang in Banggai language). Miraculously, swift water gushed from the ground, eventually flooding the entire wedding area. This puddle was named Lemelu after the girl promised to Anggabule. Then, Anggabule ran to high ground remembering his mother's message: 'Run to the mountains and don't look back.' However, upon hearing the sound of water and dog barks, Anggabule looked back. Instantly, he turned into a wild areca nut tree (odion), which bleeds sap like blood when its trunk is slashed. Before fleeing, Anggabule released a bat from the basket, telling it to pass this story to Lemelu's family. The bat flew far and dropped its waste in various places, including Lelau, Tetean, Bubunit, Bundala, Keubilito, and Ebunga. The bat's droppings formed puddles of water. These puddles are named after people. The Bubunit puddle merged with Bundala, now known as Bundala, the tourist spot Lake Bundala Alani. This legend lives in the memory of the community and becomes an inseparable part of the cultural and natural landscape in Banggai Kepulauan.
wisata.excerpt.sumur-oang: Behind the dense forest of Sambulangan Village, there is a large vertical hole long known by the community as O'ang Well. Its location is hidden...
wisata.description.sumur-oang: Behind the dense forest of Sambulangan Village, there is a large vertical hole long known by the community as O'ang Well. Its location is hidden from the main road and its existence was only discovered around 1956-1957, when a local family began opening a garden in the area. When discovered, the well's shape was the same as it is today, a vertical hole with stagnant water at the bottom. 'O'ang' comes from a local term meaning a fallen cave or a cavity collapsed inward. This name arose from the natural shape of the well resembling a large vertical hole, as if the ground above had sunk and formed an open space downward.
wisata.excerpt.tari-balatindak: Balatindak Dance is one of the traditional dances of the Banggai tribe originating from Banggai Kepulauan Regency, Central Sulawesi. Originally...
wisata.description.tari-balatindak: Balatindak Dance is one of the traditional dances of the Banggai tribe originating from Banggai Kepulauan Regency, Central Sulawesi. Originally, Balatindak Dance was known as a war dance or soldiery dance of the Banggai tribe. The word 'Balatindak' itself comes from the Banggai language consisting of two syllables: 'ba' meaning repeatedly, and 'tindak' meaning stomping feet. This depicts the stomping foot movements, showing the spirit of bravery and agility in facing enemies. Over time, Balatindak Dance evolved into a dance welcoming important guests. This dance became a form of respect and warm welcome to arriving guests.

wisata.excerpt.liang-molopo: In the Banggai language, “Liang” means cave, while “Molopo” means collapsed—describing the shape of the cave formed by natural rock falls and soil weathering...
wisata.description.liang-molopo: In the Banggai language, “Liang” means cave, while “Molopo” means collapsed—describing the shape of the cave formed by natural rock falls and soil weathering. According to the stories passed down through generations, Liang Molopo used to be a place for meditation and reflection for the ancestors of the Buko Village community. Liang Molopo is located in the Tobusang Hamlet area which holds historical stories. In the past, this area was part of the Dallu Kingdom, a kingdom famous for its natural wealth, especially gold nuggets. This wealth became the reason for the outbreak of a conflict with the Banggai Kingdom, which eventually attacked Dallu to seize the treasure. When the battle reached its peak and the Dallu troops were on the verge of defeat, King Dallu did something extraordinary—he stepped on the Abu Matano (sacred kitchen ash) with full conviction. Instantly, a thick fog enveloped the battlefield and the King mysteriously disappeared, never to be seen again. Since then, the Dallu Kingdom ended, and the legend of the disappearing King became a story in the lives of the Buko community. It is said that inside this cave there is a container formerly kept by King Dallu as a place to store heirlooms or important kingdom relics. This chest is guarded by unseen guardians, invisible beings believed to be ancestral spirits or guardians of the sacred area. The peak of Liang Molopo is a sacred place for the surrounding community. In the past, this place was often used to meditate and ask for guidance from ancestral spirits, especially during disease outbreaks, disasters, or rampant crimes. In their tradition, the spirits of the ancestors are believed to still protect the descendants and the land they inherited. As a form of respect for the ancestors, people used to often place offerings around the cave.
wisata.excerpt.tari-basalendeng: Etymologically, 'Basalendeng' comes from the Banggai language. The word 'ba' means 'repeatedly', while 'salendeng' refers to 'shawl'. So...
wisata.description.tari-basalendeng: Etymologically, 'Basalendeng' comes from the Banggai language. The word 'ba' means 'repeatedly', while 'salendeng' refers to 'shawl'. So literally, Basalendeng means dancing the shawl repeatedly. This is in accordance with the main movement of the dance which indeed involves the use of a shawl as an important property. Initially, Basalendeng Dance was an entertainment dance in the Banggai royal palace environment. This dance was usually danced by noble princesses or selected dancers to entertain the king, royal relatives, and important guests. Until now, Basalendeng Dance is often used to welcome guests of honor, both from government and traditional guests.

wisata.description.pantai-pasir-putih-pu: This beach with a stretch of white sand and clear sea water is the main attraction of Sambulangan Village marine tourism. Access is via a small boat from the Sambulangan pier to Tambalang Island.
wisata.excerpt.bubung-babasal: Bubung Babasal is a body of water shaped like a large hole filled with water. Inside there is a unique phenomenon of wood rotating following...
wisata.description.bubung-babasal: Bubung Babasal is a body of water shaped like a large hole filled with water. Inside there is a unique phenomenon of wood rotating following the direction of the sun, although the wood is not always visible. Below the water surface, there are about 19 underwater 'rooms'. Some of them emit gas like smoke which has not been scientifically identified by laboratories in Indonesia. This area has also been released with various types of ornamental fish, and uniquely, leaves that fall into the water will remain intact and not change color, as if not undergoing decay. To explore this underwater room requires special skills, such as the ability to dive using ropes and cave diving techniques.

wisata.excerpt.paisu-batango: Discussing the history of Paisu Batango cannot be separated from the origins of the early naming of Luwuk Panenteng Village. In the oral tradition passed down...
wisata.description.paisu-batango: Discussing the history of Paisu Batango cannot be separated from the origins of the early naming of Luwuk Panenteng Village. In the oral tradition passed down through generations, it is told that long ago lived a mother with her child in an area passed by a river stream. The mother is believed to be the daughter of the King of Banggai. Once, her child cried incessantly and would not calm down, even though given physical comfort and rocked with love. After paying attention, it turned out the cause of the child's crying was the roar of the river water flowing swiftly around their residence. Feeling disturbed and unable to bear seeing her child unable to sleep, the loving mother made an unusual decision: she wanted to move the water flow. Before doing so, she first took as much water as possible and stored it in various containers she owned as an act of readiness so that later her family would not lack water. After that, the mother uttered a sentence in the Banggai language that sounded: 'Ko paisu no kon Sulu mbali Simpong maka mu dungol', which means, 'O water, go or move to Simpong.' In the beliefs of the Banggai people, the words of the ancestors have spiritual power and their own sacredness. So since then, the water flow is believed to move around until it finally settled in the Simpong area, Luwuk. Meanwhile, the water previously collected and stored by the mother then formed a number of paisu (waters) scattered in the Lukpanenteng Village area, including Paisu Batango, Paisu Tumundo, and Paisu Mandauling. One trusted local source stated that in the past there was a river flow path that geologically connected the Simpong area with Lukpanenteng Village. Although currently the flow has dried up, the remnants of its path can still be traced and are believed to empty around the Paisu Batango area. The naming of Paisu Batango comes from the word 'batang', but not in the general sense as in Indonesian which refers to a tree trunk. In the context of Banggai language and culture, batang has a deeper meaning, namely 'source' or 'center of origin'. Although literally different, this term still has a symbolic connection in meaning. Just as a tree trunk which is the core of the plant and has many branches in the form of twigs, Paisu Batango is also described as the main source of water flow that has several branches. This is in line with the community's belief that the swift river flow, as mentioned in local folklore, comes from Paisu Batango and then flows in various directions, resembling the structure of a tree trunk with its twigs. This naming not only contains geographic meaning, but also symbolic. In daily life from generation to generation of the Lukpanenteng Village community, Paisu Batango is seen as the source of life. Water from this Batango is used for various basic needs such as bathing, washing, cooking, to being consumed as drinking water. Therefore, the value of Paisu Batango as a source does not only refer to its physical function as a spring, but also to its vital role in supporting the survival and culture of the community from generation to generation. However, until now there are still differences of opinion among the community regarding whether the flowing water referred to in this story refers to Paisu Batango or other paisu. This story is compiled based on narratives that developed in the community, so it is open to the possibility of different versions.
wisata.excerpt.paisu-pok: The story behind the name and existence of Paisu Pok has several versions circulating orally among the community, but one of the most p...
wisata.description.paisu-pok: The story behind the name and existence of Paisu Pok has several versions circulating orally among the community, but one of the most popular is the story about a princess's wedding. According to local residents, a very festive royal wedding was once held, lasting seven days and seven nights. At that time, people's houses were still stilt houses built of wood and bamboo. The festivity was accompanied by traditional musical instruments like drums, played along with the traditional Salendeng Dance. Not only dancers, but guests also joined in dancing to the drum rhythm echoing throughout the village. The atmosphere was so lively that even simple tools like pongisuk—a stick used to check the doneness of food in the wok—danced along to the drumbeat. Because the floor was made of wooden planks with gaps, the swaying pongisuk jumped between the boards without human touch. This phenomenon was so rare and unusual that it sparked laughter from the community watching it. However, the laughter was considered a violation of traditional norms, known locally as a pamali (taboo) act. It is said that due to this disrespectful attitude, a massive tornado appeared, sweeping and spinning everything around it—humans, houses, and trees. The disaster left a large hole filled with debris like tree trunks, roots, rocks, and other ruins. This hole then filled with water and is known today as Paisu Pok. Etymologically, in the Banggai language, paisu means water, and pok means black. Sources state the name arose because the water reflects a black color due to moss-covered tree trunks at the bottom. Historically, however, the name Pok comes from the princess's name—Muluko Mupok, an exotic dark-skinned woman known to be very beautiful and graceful. From her name, the site was named Paisu Pok, symbolically meaning the 'water' attached to Princess Mupok's name.

kegiatan.title.kilau-samudra-lestari: Kilau Samudra Lestari Enlivens Conservation and Marine Tourism in Lukpanenteng
kegiatan.excerpt.kilau-samudra-lestari: Kilau Samudra Lestari in Lukpanenteng Village combines diving training, marine conservation, and marine tourism promotion. Initiated by KKN-PPM UGM 2025 together with the government and community.
kegiatan.description.kilau-samudra-lesta:
Lukpanenteng, Banggai Kepulauan – Lukpanenteng Village, North Bulagi District, hosted Kilau Samudra Lestari on July 25-27, 2025, combining diving training, conservation education, and marine tourism promotion.

For Lukpanenteng residents, swimming and diving have become part of daily life. With its wealth of coral reefs and natural dive spots, the village has the potential to become a center for marine education and tourism, although capacity constraints remain a challenge.

The 2025 UGM Banggai Kepulauan KKN-PPM team collaborated with the village government, local community, and marine conservation partners, including Sentra Selam Jogja, to provide community-based training. 'This activity is important to raise community awareness about protecting the sea while serving as a forum for local capacity building,' said the Secretary of North Bulagi District.

The series of activities included: Basic water rescue training by Dr. James H. Pinontoan, Head of the Banggai Kepulauan Tourism Office; SKKNI-based snorkeling guide certification with Sentra Selam Jogja; Education on the dangers of destructive fishing guided by Blue Alliance; Exploration of dive spots by the Tourism Office and KKN-PPM UGM students.

Participants consisted of students, local youth, agency representatives, and conservation partner organizations. Blue Alliance accompanied the training while strengthening the narrative of coastal ecosystem protection, emphasizing that effective conservation is born from community collaboration and research-based academic understanding.

Besides training and conservation actions, this activity also served as a promotional medium for dive spots through visual documentation and ocean awareness campaigns. 'This activity is a form of synergy between students, the government, and village residents in protecting the sea. We hope this activity continues every year,' said Adiliyansyah, Chairman of the 2025 Kilau Samudra Lestari Committee.

Lukpanenteng is now known not only as a charming dive destination, but also as a village that has begun building the future of its sea with the hands and spirit of its own residents.
kegiatan.title.festival-sea-sea-2025: Sea-Sea Festival 2025 Brings Banggai Kepulauan Coastal Culture to Life
kegiatan.excerpt.festival-sea-sea-2025: Sea-Sea Festival 2025 in Sambulangan Village presents coastal cultural festivities with traditional competitions, folk arts, and the inauguration of the Lukpanenteng Diving Center and O'ang Basal access.
kegiatan.description.festival-sea-sea-20:
Banggai Kepulauan – Applause and laughter broke the morning silence in Sambulangan Village, North Bulagi. The 2025 Sea-Sea Festival officially opened on August 3, marking a week of festivities blending tradition, sports, and coastal community togetherness.

From day one, traditional competitions to modern sports rolled interchangeably. Sack races, tug-of-war, rowing, to men's and women's volleyball drew cheers from the crowd. Regional competitions like baode and storytelling became the spotlight, reviving the collective memory of Banggai's cultural heritage. Ten MSME booths showcased flagship products, from seafood to handicrafts.

The climax on August 9 was festive. Cooking competitions, MSME exhibitions, and village art performances filled the stage alternately. Folk music played during the announcement of competition winners, followed by the Badero dance which strengthened togetherness. UGM KKN-PPM students, residents, and guests held hands, dancing together as a symbol of cross-age and professional unity.

'The 2025 Sea-Sea Festival went smoothly. Seeing all elements of society, from children to parents, actively participating and enjoying this event, I feel proud and inspired. This festival is not just entertainment, but also our way of strengthening coastal cultural identity and fostering a spirit of togetherness. Hopefully, this spirit continues to live and becomes an annual tradition awaited by the community,' said Dio, Chairman of the 2025 Sea-Sea Festival Committee.

The Sea-Sea Festival proves that cultural preservation and economic development can go hand in hand.

Banggai Kepulauan – The 2025 Sea-Sea Festival not only enlivened the coast with folk competitions and arts, but also marked a new chapter in marine tourism development. On August 9, 2025, two flagship facilities officially opened: the Lukpanenteng Diving Center and access road to O'ang Basal Sambulangan.

The inauguration was carried out by the Deputy Regent of Banggai Kepulauan, accompanied by the Head of the Tourism Office and village government representatives. Dozens of residents, tourism actors, and UGM KKN-PPM students witnessed this historic moment.

The Lukpanenteng Diving Center, which has been under construction since 2018, is equipped with an equipment storage room, a basic training area, and a small pier for tourist boats. This facility opens up opportunities for local snorkeling guides and diving instructors.

Meanwhile, O'ang Basal is a natural karst phenomenon in the form of a giant hole 20 meters wide, 50 meters long, and with a mouth area of approximately 675 square meters. The newly inaugurated road makes it easier for tourists and researchers to access while supporting conservation-based geotourism development.

The inauguration of these two facilities is a symbol of collaboration between the government, community, and academics. In the context of the 2025 Sea-Sea Festival, both are not just new infrastructure, but proof of the commitment to protecting the sea, preserving coastal culture, and building a sustainable future for Banggai Kepulauan tourism.
kegiatan.title.fun-triathlon-2025: Regent of Bangkep Inaugurates Fun Triathlon 2025 in Bungin
kegiatan.excerpt.fun-triathlon-2025: Banggai Kepulauan Regent Rusli Moidady inaugurated the Fun Triathlon 2025 in Bungin Village with the theme 'Run, Ride, Discover – Exploring the Beauty of Banggai Island!'.
kegiatan.description.fun-triathlon-2025:
Bungin – Sunday (20/07/2025), the Regent of Banggai Kepulauan Rusli Moidady, ST., MT., opened the 2025 Fun Triathlon with the theme 'Run, Ride, Discover – Exploring the Beauty of Banggai Island!' at the Bungin Village field. This event serves as a forum for collaboration between the local government, village government, KKN students, and the community to promote tourism and healthy living.

The triathlon involves swimming 100 m, cycling 14 km, and running 7 km. In addition, there was a children's coloring contest and a local MSME bazaar. 'This is not just sports, but a form of fun tourism promotion and building healthy lifestyle habits,' said the Regent.

KKN students played an active role from planning to the day of the event. 'When the activity took place in Bungin Village, our involvement was not limited to administrative roles, but also included decision making and execution in the field. We had to ensure every segment of the event went according to plan,' added Merisa, Chairperson of the 2025 Fun Triathlon Committee.

The Regent hopes this event becomes a momentum for sustainable collaboration and can be developed into a national event. 'Activities like this are easier to run if carried out together, with a spirit of mutual cooperation,' he concluded.

The 2025 Fun Triathlon proves that collaboration between the government, students, and the community can elevate Banggai Kepulauan to the national stage, while promoting tourism and a healthy lifestyle.
kegiatan.title.peluncuran-dokumen-warisa: Launch of the 2025 Banggai Kepulauan Heritage Document
kegiatan.excerpt.peluncuran-dokumen-wari: The 2025 UGM KKN-PPM team launched the website and book 'Banggai Kepulauan Heritage Document', containing history, traditions, culinary, and tourism from six KKN villages.
kegiatan.description.peluncuran-dokumen-:
Banggai Kepulauan Regency, Central Sulawesi – The 2025 UGM KKN-PPM team launched the 'Banggai Kepulauan Heritage Document' website and a cultural documentation book from six KKN village locations: Buko, Lumbi-Lumbia, Sambulangan, Lukpanenteng, Bungin, and Bakalan.

This website and book present information about history, traditions, culinary, flora-fauna, and local tourist destinations, serving as a reference for the community, tourists, and tour guides.

This documentation focuses on three main aspects, namely:

History and culture of each village

Typical culinary and family medicinal plants

Flora, fauna, and tourist destinations along with their facilities

'With the presence of the Banggai Kepulauan Heritage Document, we hope to preserve local culture while providing information that is easily accessible to the wider community,' said Angga, Student Coordinator of the 2025 UGM Banggai Kepulauan KKN-PPM.

The supervising lecturer, Drs. Hendrie Adji Kusworo, M.Sc., Ph.D., added that this initiative could serve as an example of a KKN program based on cultural and environmental preservation.

The official website can be accessed through the Banggai Kepulauan KKN-UGM platform @pengabdikebanggaan.
